subject: Intro / Discovery — latency & concurrency goals (Finly)
messages:
From: Tom Garcia <tom@finly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Discovery — latency & concurrency goals

Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro call today — this was super helpful. Quick recap from our side and the areas we need to validate before we can commit to a PoC / budget:  

Pain points
- Streaming UX is poor: users see a big pause before the first tokens render, which hurts conversions. Goal is sub-300ms first-byte p95 for short prompts (<= 64 tokens).
- p95 tail latency for full responses is currently ~1.8s on our hosted provider for standard prompt families; spikes to >3s under modest load.
- Concurrency: we need to support ~200 concurrent live users during peak (with average session generating ~3 requests/min).
- Cost: token spend and egress are a concern — we need predictable unit economics.

Current stack
- Frontend streaming via SSE, backend on GCP running a mix of hosted API calls and a small self-hosted LLM for cheaper, low-priority tasks.
- No centralized KV cache for prefixes; little request-level batching today.

Success criteria for an initial PoC
- First-byte p95 <= 300ms for streaming on the client for short prompts.
- End-to-end p95 <= 700ms for typical assistant responses (<=256 tokens) under target concurrency.
- 99.9% availability during test window.
- Clear cost projection for production traffic (tokens / GPU hours).

Next steps
- Can you send a short written recap and a proposed benchmarking plan (what we'll measure and what data you need from us)?
- We'll provision a test account and share API keys / sample prompt sets if that helps.

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Happy to loop in our infra lead if you need additional telemetry.

—Tom
Tom Garcia
VP Engineering, Finly
tom@finly.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Tom Garcia <tom@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Discovery — latency & concurrency goals

Tom — thanks for the clear notes, and great meeting today. Below is a concise recap and our proposed next steps / benchmark plan. I've attached a short proposal and a benchmarking worksheet.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary pain: poor streaming first-byte and tail p95s impacting conversion. Target first-byte p95 <= 300ms for short prompts; overall p95 <= 700ms for <=256-token responses.
- Concurrency target: ~200 concurrent live users (estimate ~3 reqs/min per user on avg during peak).
- Current architecture: frontend streams via SSE; backend mixes hosted API and a self-hosted model on GCP; no persistent prefix KV cache and limited batching.
- Cost sensitivity around tokens and GPU usage; need predictable unit economics.

Success criteria (PoC)
- Measured client first-byte p95 <= 300ms under simulated production load for short prompts (<=64 tokens).
- End-to-end p95 <= 700ms for typical assistant flows (<=256 tokens) under target concurrency.
- Demonstrated improvement in P95 tail vs current provider and a cost projection.

Proposed benchmark plan (attached: benchmark-plan.xlsx) — high level
- Test harness: we'll run a replay of your sampled prompt set (you can redact PII) with two load profiles: baseline (50 concurrent users) and peak (200 concurrent users).
- Measurements collected: client-first-byte timing, server token generation latency, per-request token counts, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates.
- Streaming specifics: measure time to first token delivered to the client, and percent of requests that stream vs single-chunk responses.
- Failure modes: evaluate behavior when capacity constrained (queue times, graceful fallback to smaller model variant).

Next steps / asks from Finly
1) Share a sample prompt set + expected token lengths (redact anything sensitive).
2) Provide a short window for the PoC test (we suggest a 48-72 hour synthetic run during a representative traffic window).
3) Temporary API keys / sandbox access for us to run the harness.

What we'll deliver
- A short report with p95 measurements, cost estimates (tokens & GPU hours), suggested runtime config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization profile), and a recommended deployment path (hosted vs dedicated).
- A proposed mutual action plan and timeline for a 4-6 week PoC if metrics look good.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf, benchmark-plan.xlsx

If you're good with that, Marissa / Dev and I will get a test run scheduled. I'll also put together an initial config suggestion for streaming (kernel / batch sizing / cache hints) for Dev to review.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Discovery — latency & concurrency goals (internal)

Looping internally — quick asks for the PoC prep:  
- Dev: can you review the benchmark-plan.xlsx and confirm the streaming measurement hooks (client-first-byte, server gen latency, KV hit metrics) + estimate how long a 200-concurrency synthetic run will need on our infra?
- Aditya: please draft the mutual action plan (milestones + owners) and a rough cost estimate for a 4-week dedicated PoC vs hosted burst model.
- I'll prepare the SOW / pricing outline once we have the benchmark numbers.

Also flagging potential upsell angle: if we can demonstrably hit the first-byte target, we should propose a small dedicated pool + prefix cache to lock in predictable latency.

Thanks — will be on standby for the sample prompt set from Tom.

—Marissa
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Aditya — this looks great, thanks for the rapid follow-up and the attachments. We'll:  
- Share a redacted prompt set and a 48-hour window next week for the synthetic run.
- Provision sandbox API keys (security will coordinate) and share them with you and your infra contact.
- Tentatively booked a follow-up to review results on Tue, 28 Mar at 10:00 PT — can you and Marissa make that?

We care most about the streaming first-byte experience — if you can show a consistent win there and a reasonable cost profile, we'll move to a short-term pilot.

Thanks — Tom
